recommendation: Keep this audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-19823 unless a future work group decision changes the search parameter code, type, or expression.
issue_request: FHIR-19823 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked for a DocumentReference search parameter named "creation" of type date over content.attachment.creation, because DocumentReference.date records the metadata creation time rather than the underlying document attachment creation time.
initial_application: The issue was applied in PR 716 by git commit 24ebc2aadefd4ba91d3d5380d091e15c61a202e2, which added a creation/date search-parameter row with expression DocumentReference.content.attachment.creation to the then-authoritative DocumentReference spreadsheet. The 2021 source rework commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 carried that row into the current XML search-parameter bundle.
additional_context: DocumentReference is active in source/fhir.ini, and the current combined branch source contains SearchParameter DocumentReference-creation with code creation, type date, and expression DocumentReference.content.attachment.creation. The same PR 716 and OO block vote also covered nearby DocumentReference search-parameter issue FHIR-19860, which is already represented on the combined branch. FHIR-3478 is relevant background because it introduced Attachment.creation, and it is also already represented on the combined branch. Zulip and Confluence block-vote evidence supports the Jira disposition, and no later conflicting decision was found in the bounded source/community/history checks.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current build-scope source already contains the requested DocumentReference creation search parameter.

related_jiras.note: The same PR 716 application commit and OO block vote added the neighboring DocumentReference doc-status search parameter, and that issue is already represented on the combined branch.
The earlier Attachment.creation datatype issue established the field that this search parameter indexes, and that issue is already represented on the combined branch.
